name: SOL plain open reversal
description: SOL: right after a 15-minute window opens, if the previous window moved more than 1.25 of its usual standard deviations, buy the reversal side (taker, hold to settlement). Plain version of sol-volrev/sol-midrev without their volume or last-5-minute filters, so it trades about 3x as often and needs no flow stream.
hypothesis: Short-horizon crypto returns reverse after big moves (sign autocorrelation -0.02..-0.09 every month), Kalshi's opening quote treats the window as a coin flip. Screens say the edge decayed on all coins in May-Aug, but ad hoc engine runs of the plain rule on 2-week SOL windows (Feb-Aug) net +0.6..+7c/ct after fees, so the question is whether the plain rule on SOL alone (never run through the pipeline) clears CI>0 with enough trades (~170/month). Losers: opening takers/quoters. A post-only entry (maker=1) was tested ad hoc and adds nothing measurable (adverse selection offsets the saved fee). Wrong if: full CI<=0, <60% months positive, 2x latency loses, or lockbox loses.
next: rejected at lockbox (-0.36c); edge decayed since June
